opening.text: Imagine a letter that was promised a long time ago. A friend wrote, “I will come. Watch for me.” Years pass. Then more years. Some people stop watching. Others keep the porch light on. And then one night, the door opens, and the friend is standing there, just as promised.
That is what the birth of Jesus Christ was for the world. It was a promise kept. Prophets had spoken of it for centuries. And one night in a small town, it happened.
Today I want to talk about His birth. Not just the story we know, but what it means.

mainMessage.text: Jesus Christ was born in Bethlehem, to Mary, a young woman of Nazareth. His Father was God. His mother was mortal. He was born in the lowest of places, and angels told shepherds first. He came because the Father loves us, and He came to rescue us. His birth is the beginning of the most important story ever told. And it was not an accident. It was the keeping of a promise.

blocks.text: The promise was made long before.

Prophets in the Old Testament spoke of a child who would be born. Isaiah called Him by great names. Micah named the town where He would come from. These words were written hundreds of years before the night in Bethlehem.

For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.

But thou, Beth-lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.

Notice the last words of Micah: “from of old, from everlasting.” The child in the manger was not new. The First Presidency and the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in “The Living Christ: The Testimony of the Apostles,” given on January 1, 2000.

We solemnly testify that His life, which is central to all human history, neither began in Bethlehem nor concluded on Calvary. He was the Firstborn of the Father, the Only Begotten Son in the flesh, the Redeemer of the world.
He lived before He was born. He was the Firstborn of the Father. That makes the promise even more wonderful.
He was born of Mary, and He was the Son of God.

The angel Gabriel came to a young woman in Nazareth. He told her something no one had ever heard. Mary asked an honest question. The angel gave her an honest answer. About eighty years earlier, the prophet Alma had told the people in the Americas the same thing.

And the angel said unto her, Fear not, Mary: for thou hast found favour with God. And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name Jesus. He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David: And he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and of his kingdom there shall be no end. Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man? And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.

And behold, he shall be born of Mary, at Jerusalem which is the land of our forefathers, she being a virgin, a precious and chosen vessel, who shall be overshadowed and conceive by the power of the Holy Ghost, and bring forth a son, yea, even the Son of God.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles explained why this matters in his talk “The Atonement” from the October 1996 general conference.
Jesus was the only one who could offer such an infinite atonement, since He was born of a mortal mother and an immortal Father. Because of that unique birthright, Jesus was an infinite Being.
From Mary He had a mortal body. From God He had divine power. Both were needed.
He was born in the humblest place.

You would expect a king to be born in a palace. This King was not. Joseph and Mary traveled to Bethlehem because of a tax. There was no room for them at the inn. The first bed He ever had was a feeding trough for animals.

And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judaea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem; (because he was of the house and lineage of David:) To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child. And so it was, that, while they were there, the days were accomplished that she should be delivered. And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.
The First Presidency and the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles opened “The Living Christ: The Testimony of the Apostles” on January 1, 2000, with these words.

As we commemorate the birth of Jesus Christ two millennia ago, we offer our testimony of the reality of His matchless life and the infinite virtue of His great atoning sacrifice. None other has had so profound an influence upon all who have lived and will yet live upon the earth.
The humblest birth. The greatest influence. That is how He works.
The news went first to shepherds.

Shepherds were not important people. They worked at night. They smelled like sheep. Yet when God sent His angels to announce the birth, He sent them to the fields. Heaven told the ordinary people first.

And there were in the same country shepherds abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night. And, lo, the angel of the Lord came upon them, and the glory of the Lord shone round about them: and they were sore afraid. And the angel said unto them, Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people. For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord. And this shall be a sign unto you; Ye shall find the babe wrapped in swaddling clothes, lying in a manger. And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host praising God, and saying, Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.

The baby in that manger was no ordinary child. The First Presidency and the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said who He was in “The Living Christ: The Testimony of the Apostles,” given on January 1, 2000.
He was the Great Jehovah of the Old Testament, the Messiah of the New. Under the direction of His Father, He was the creator of the earth.
The Creator of the earth, wrapped in swaddling clothes. The angel said the news was for “all people.” That includes you.
Heaven gave signs across the world.

The birth of Jesus was not only noticed in Bethlehem. A new star appeared in the east, and wise men followed it. On the other side of the world, in the Americas, the prophet Samuel the Lamanite had told the people of a sign. It all happened, just as promised.

Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judaea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem, Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him.

And behold, he said unto them: Behold, I give unto you a sign; for five years more cometh, and behold, then cometh the Son of God to redeem all those who shall believe on his name. And behold, this will I give unto you for a sign at the time of his coming; for behold, there shall be great lights in heaven, insomuch that in the night before he cometh there shall be no darkness, insomuch that it shall appear unto man as if it was day. Therefore, there shall be one day and a night and a day, as if it were one day and there were no night; and this shall be unto you for a sign; for ye shall know of the rising of the sun and also of its setting; therefore they shall know of a surety that there shall be two days and a night; nevertheless the night shall not be darkened; and it shall be the night before he is born. And behold, there shall a new star arise, such an one as ye never have beheld; and this also shall be a sign unto you. And behold this is not all, there shall be many signs and wonders in heaven.

Lift up your head and be of good cheer; for behold, the time is at hand, and on this night shall the sign be given, and on the morrow come I into the world, to show unto the world that I will fulfil all that which I have caused to be spoken by the mouth of my holy prophets.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles taught about the Savior’s unique parentage in his talk “Constancy amid Change” from the October 1993 general conference.

According to eternal law, that atonement required a personal sacrifice by an immortal being not subject to death. Yet He must die and take up His own body again. The Savior was the only one who could accomplish this. From His mother He inherited power to die. From His Father He obtained power over death.
The signs were for the world. The birth was for the world. The sacrifice that came later was for the world.
He came to save us.

It is a beautiful thing to celebrate a birth. But Christmas is only the beginning of the story. King Benjamin’s angel told him why the Lord would come. He would live among us, heal us, and suffer for us.

For behold, the time cometh, and is not far distant, that with power, the Lord Omnipotent who reigneth, who was, and is from all eternity to all eternity, shall come down from heaven among the children of men, and shall dwell in a tabernacle of clay, and shall go forth amongst men, working mighty miracles, such as healing the sick, raising the dead, causing the lame to walk, the blind to receive their sight, and the deaf to hear, and curing all manner of diseases. And he shall cast out devils, or the evil spirits which dwell in the hearts of the children of men. And lo, he shall suffer temptations, and pain of body, hunger, thirst, and fatigue, even more than man can suffer, except it be unto death; for behold, blood cometh from every pore, so great shall be his anguish for the wickedness and the abominations of his people. And he shall be called Jesus Christ, the Son of God, the Father of heaven and earth, the Creator of all things from the beginning; and his mother shall be called Mary.
Elder Bruce R. McConkie of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles wrote this in his book The Mortal Messiah (1979).
The condescension of God lies in the fact that he, an exalted Being, steps down from his eternal throne to become the Father of a mortal Son.
The word “condescension” means a willing step down. God did not have to. He chose to, because He loves us.

story.title: The shepherds go to Bethlehem

blocks.text: After the angels left, the shepherds could have stayed with their sheep. They had a long night ahead. They did not. They said to each other, “Let us go.”

And it came to pass, as the angels were gone away from them into heaven, the shepherds said one to another, Let us now go even unto Bethlehem, and see this thing which is come to pass, which the Lord hath made known unto us. And they came with haste, and found Mary, and Joseph, and the babe lying in a manger.
They came with haste. They did not wait for a better time. When heaven calls, they went. I think about how many times I have put off something the Lord asked me to do. The shepherds teach me to go.

application.text: First, this season or this week, read Luke 2 slowly, out loud, with your family or alone. Let the words do their work. Second, think of one person who may feel overlooked, like the shepherds. Give them some of your time. Third, ask yourself what gift He would want from you. It might be forgiveness, patience, or a kind word.

opening.text: There is an old kind of story about a prince who leaves the palace. He puts on plain clothes. He walks the streets and works beside ordinary people. He eats their food and learns their names. He does it because he wants to know what life is like for those he will one day rule.
It is only a story. But it points to something real. A King did come down. He did not hide who He was out of curiosity. He came to lift us up.
I want to talk about the birth of Jesus Christ, and what it cost Him to come.

mainMessage.text: The Son of God left His Father’s presence and was born as a baby, to a mortal mother, in a stable. He was announced by angels, and He was worshipped by shepherds and by wise men. His coming had been promised for centuries, and on the other side of the world, signs were given too. Every part of the story shows how much the Father and the Son love us. They sent the best they had.

blocks.text: He was promised, and He was older than His birth.
Isaiah wrote of a child who would be given. Micah said where He would come from. Both prophets saw something larger than a baby. They saw a ruler whose “goings forth have been from of old.”

For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.

Before He was a baby, He was God’s firstborn. Before the manger, there was a throne.
His mother was mortal. His Father was God.

Mary was young. She was surprised and afraid. But she listened, and she asked the angel how it would happen. The answer was holy and simple. Alma said it, too, when he taught the people in the Americas.

And the angel said unto her, Fear not, Mary: for thou hast found favour with God. And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name Jesus. Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man? And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.

And behold, he shall be born of Mary, at Jerusalem which is the land of our forefathers, she being a virgin, a precious and chosen vessel, who shall be overshadowed and conceive by the power of the Holy Ghost, and bring forth a son, yea, even the Son of God.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Atonement” from the October 1996 general conference.
Jesus was the only one who could offer such an infinite atonement, since He was born of a mortal mother and an immortal Father. Because of that unique birthright, Jesus was an infinite Being.
He understood our mortal life because He lived it. He had divine power because He was God’s Son. He was both, and He used both to bless us.
The King had no room at the inn.

The journey to Bethlehem was not easy. It was about ninety miles from Nazareth, and Mary was expecting. When they arrived, there was nowhere to stay. In the end, the Son of God was laid where the animals ate.

And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judaea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem; (because he was of the house and lineage of David:) To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child. And so it was, that, while they were there, the days were accomplished that she should be delivered. As we commemorate the birth of Jesus Christ two millennia ago, we offer our testimony of the reality of His matchless life and the infinite virtue of His great atoning sacrifice. None other has had so profound an influence upon all who have lived and will yet live upon the earth.
No room at the inn. Yet no one has had a greater influence on the world. He needs no palace to be great.
Angels sang to ordinary people.
On a quiet hillside, a few tired shepherds suddenly saw the sky fill with light. They were afraid. The angel told them not to be. He had good news, and it was meant for everyone.

And there were in the same country shepherds abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night. The One who made the hills the shepherds stood on was now a baby in a trough. And the first people to hear were the ones no one else noticed.
The whole world was given a sign.

In the east, wise men saw a new star and traveled far to find Him. In the Americas, believers watched for a night with no darkness. The same Lord was announcing the same birth to people who had never met. That is how large His birth was.

Therefore, there shall be one day and a night and a day, as if it were one day and there were no night; and this shall be unto you for a sign; for ye shall know of the rising of the sun and also of its setting; therefore they shall know of a surety that there shall be two days and a night; nevertheless the night shall not be darkened; and it shall be the night before he is born. The Savior was the only one who could accomplish this. From His mother He inherited power to die. From His Father He obtained power over death.
The Lord told the faithful that He would come. Then He came. Every sign came true.
He came down to lift us up.
King Benjamin was taught by an angel what the Lord’s mission would be. The Lord would live among people. He would heal. He would suffer. And it would all start with a mother named Mary.

For behold, the time cometh, and is not far distant, that with power, the Lord Omnipotent who reigneth, who was, and is from all eternity to all eternity, shall come down from heaven among the children of men, and shall dwell in a tabernacle of clay, and shall go forth amongst men, working mighty miracles, such as healing the sick, raising the dead, causing the lame to walk, the blind to receive their sight, and the deaf to hear, and curing all manner of diseases. And he shall cast out devils, or the evil spirits which dwell in the hearts of the children of men. And lo, he shall suffer temptations, and pain of body, hunger, thirst, and fatigue, even more than man can suffer, except it be unto death; for behold, blood cometh from every pore, so great shall be his anguish for the wickedness and the abominations of his people. The condescension of God lies in the fact that he, an exalted Being, steps down from his eternal throne to become the Father of a mortal Son.
He did not have to come. He stepped down on purpose. That is the meaning of Christmas.

story.title: The wise men find the child

blocks.text: The wise men followed a star for a long way. They came into Jerusalem, and then Bethlehem. At last, the star stood still over a house. They had come to the right place.

When they had heard the king, they departed; and, lo, the star, which they saw in the east, went before them, till it came and stood over where the young child was. When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy. And when they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother, and fell down, and worshipped him: and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.
Two things stand out. They rejoiced with exceeding great joy. And they fell down and worshipped. Joy and worship are good ways to meet the Savior.

application.text: First, pick one way to worship Him this week that has nothing to do with gifts. It might be a quiet hymn, a prayer on your knees, or time at the temple. Second, think about what you would give if you were with the wise men. Then give a version of it to someone who needs it. Third, tell one person why the birth of Jesus matters to you. Keep it short and true.

The night Jesus was born was a night like that for the world. The world was dark in many ways. And then a light came on. It was small and quiet. A baby, in a stable. But it was the light the whole world had been waiting for.
I would like to talk about that night, and what it tells us about God.

And it was planned from the beginning.

He was truly the Son of God, and truly the son of Mary.

He came quietly.
There was no parade for His arrival, and no royal welcome. A tired couple, a crowded town, a borrowed place. Luke tells it plainly, without decoration. And that simple telling is part of its power.

His greatness did not need a grand entrance. Quiet births can change the world.
Heaven could not stay quiet.
While the world slept, heaven burst into song. The angels did not go to the temple or the palace. They went to the fields. That tells me something about whom God looks for.

Therefore, there shall be one day and a night and a day, as if it were one day and there were no night; and this shall be unto you for a sign; for ye shall know of the rising of the sun and also of its setting; therefore they shall know of a surety that there shall be two days and a night; nevertheless the night shall not be darkened; and it shall be the night before he is born. And behold, there shall a new star arise, such an one as ye never have beheld; and this also shall be a sign unto you. And behold this is not all, there shall be many signs and wonders in heaven.

Lift up your head and be of good cheer; for behold, the time is at hand, and on this night shall the sign be given, and on the morrow come I into the world, to show unto the world that I will fulfil all that which I have caused to be spoken by the mouth of my holy prophets.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Constancy amid Change” from the October 1993 general conference.

According to eternal law, that atonement required a personal sacrifice by an immortal being not subject to death. Yet He must die and take up His own body again. The Savior was the only one who could accomplish this. From His mother He inherited power to die. From His Father He obtained power over death.
He came into the world as a baby. He left it, in time, as the Savior. The two belong together.
The baby was sent to save.

story.title: Nephi sees the mother of the Son of God

blocks.text: Six hundred years before the birth of Jesus, a young man named Nephi prayed to understand his father’s dream. An angel took him in vision to Nazareth. He saw a woman. Then the angel asked him a question that I think of often.

And it came to pass that I looked and beheld the great city of Jerusalem, and also other cities. And I beheld the city of Nazareth; and in the city of Nazareth I beheld a virgin, and she was exceedingly fair and white. And it came to pass that I saw the heavens open; and an angel came down and stood before me; and he said unto me: Nephi, what beholdest thou? And I said unto him: A virgin, most beautiful and fair above all other virgins. And he said unto me: Knowest thou the condescension of God? And I said unto him: I know that he loveth his children; nevertheless, I do not know the meaning of all things. And he said unto me: Behold, the virgin whom thou seest is the mother of the Son of God, after the manner of the flesh. And it came to pass that I beheld that she was carried away in the Spirit; and after she had been carried away in the Spirit for the space of a time the angel spake unto me, saying: Look! And I looked and beheld the virgin again, bearing a child in her arms. And the angel said unto me: Behold the Lamb of God, yea, even the Son of the Eternal Father! Knowest thou the meaning of the tree which thy father saw?
Nephi did not know everything. But he knew God loved His children. That was enough to start. It is enough for us, too.

opening.text: A lifeguard cannot save a swimmer from the pool deck. He has to get wet. He has to leave the dry place, step into the water, and reach the one who is drowning. If he stays on the edge, the rescue does not happen.
That is a small picture of what the Savior did. He did not rescue us from a distance. He came down into our world. He took on a body. He was born, and He lived among us.
Today I would like to talk about His birth, and about how much He was willing to leave behind.

mainMessage.text: Jesus Christ was born in Bethlehem to Mary. His Father was God. He was announced by angels, worshipped by shepherds and wise men, and welcomed with signs in the heavens. He was born into a poor family, in a place with no room for them. He did this so He could reach us. His birth was the first step into the water.

blocks.text: He was promised from the start.
The prophets said He would come. Isaiah described Him. Micah told where He would be born. They wrote so that when He came, people would know Him.

For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.

But thou, Beth-lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.

We solemnly testify that His life, which is central to all human history, neither began in Bethlehem nor concluded on Calvary. He was the Firstborn of the Father, the Only Begotten Son in the flesh, the Redeemer of the world.
He was already the Firstborn. He chose to enter the water.
He came through Mary, and from God.

Mary heard from an angel that she would bear the Son of God. She asked how. The answer was the power of the Holy Ghost. This is a miracle we do not fully understand. But we can trust the One who told it.

And the angel said unto her, Fear not, Mary: for thou hast found favour with God. And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name Jesus. He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David: And he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and of his kingdom there shall be no end. Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man? And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.

And behold, he shall be born of Mary, at Jerusalem which is the land of our forefathers, she being a virgin, a precious and chosen vessel, who shall be overshadowed and conceive by the power of the Holy Ghost, and bring forth a son, yea, even the Son of God.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles explained it in his talk “The Atonement” from the October 1996 general conference.
Jesus was the only one who could offer such an infinite atonement, since He was born of a mortal mother and an immortal Father. Because of that unique birthright, Jesus was an infinite Being.
A mortal mother let Him feel what we feel. An immortal Father gave Him the power to save.
He was born with almost nothing.
No crib. No cradle. No room. The Savior of the world began life in the way the poorest family might. This tells us He is not far from anyone who has little.

And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judaea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem; (because he was of the house and lineage of David:) To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child. And so it was, that, while they were there, the days were accomplished that she should be delivered. And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.

The poorest start. The greatest life. There is no one who cannot take hope from that.
The angels came with good news.

The first thing the angel said to the shepherds was, “Fear not.” The first thing He said about the Savior was, “good tidings of great joy.” If we remember only one thing about the birth of Jesus, it should be the joy.

He was the Great Jehovah of the Old Testament, the Messiah of the New. Under the direction of His Father, He was the creator of the earth.
The Creator stepped into His own creation. That is a reason for joy.
The signs reached across the sea.
The star led wise men to Bethlehem. In the Americas, believers waited for a night without darkness. Many people on both sides of the world were watching. God had made sure they would know.

He came to rescue.
King Benjamin heard from an angel what the Lord would do. He would live as a man. He would heal. He would carry pain. All of it was part of the rescue.

The word is “steps down.” He did it on purpose.

story.title: The night with no darkness

blocks.text: The believers in the Americas had been waiting. Some of the people had set a date and promised to put the believers to death if the sign did not come. Then Nephi prayed, and the Lord told him the night was at hand. The sign came.

And it came to pass that there was no darkness in all that night, but it was as light as though it was mid-day. And it came to pass that the sun did rise in the morning again, according to its proper order; and they knew that it was the day that the Lord should be born, because of the sign which had been given. And it had come to pass, yea, all things, every whit, according to the words of the prophets. And it came to pass also that a new star did appear, according to the word.
The promises of God can be trusted. Every one. What He says He will do, He does.

The greatest gift ever given came that way. There was no bow. No fine paper. Just a baby, wrapped in strips of cloth, lying in a manger. If you only looked at the wrapping, you would miss it.
I want to talk about the gift of the birth of Jesus Christ, and what is inside.

Heaven announced the gift.

story.title: Mary says yes

blocks.text: Mary was young. Her life was about to change in ways she could not picture. She did not ask for proof. She did not bargain. She answered the angel with a few humble words.
And Mary said, Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word. And the angel departed from her.
After the birth, after the shepherds came and told what they had seen, Luke tells us how she took it in.
But Mary kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart.
She said yes, and then she pondered. Both are good habits. When God asks something of us, we can answer like Mary. And when He does something wonderful in our lives, we can keep it in our hearts.

application.text: First, take ten quiet minutes this week to ponder the birth of Jesus, as Mary did. Write down one thing you notice. Second, answer one small request from the Lord with a simple yes. It could be a call, a visit, or a prayer. Third, give a gift that costs you something, with no wrapping and no credit. Let it be quiet.
